title: Road accidents: reporting and police abstract — general guidance
citation: Traffic Act, Cap. 403; National Police Service guidance
content: Report accidents to police promptly, obtain the OB number and later the police abstract, and seek medical care with P3 forms where injured. Take scene photos, number plates, witness contacts, and insurance details. Insurers usually require prompt notification.

title: Drink-driving and dangerous driving — general guidance
content: Drink-driving, speeding, and dangerous driving attract fines, licence action, and possible jail terms, and weaken any civil claim. Cooperate with testing when lawfully required and seek a lawyer early. Keep the charge sheet, test records, and hearing dates.

title: Unpaid import duty and motor ownership risk — general guidance
citation: Customs law guidance; Kenya Revenue Authority guidance
content: A vehicle with unpaid duty or disputed customs clearance can be seized even if you bought it innocently. Ask for duty payment proof and verify registration details before paying. Keep duty receipts, import documents and the NTSA search result.

title: Forged or altered logbooks — general guidance
content: Forgery can involve altered names, engine numbers or fake logbook printouts, so compare the physical vehicle markings with TIMS records. Be wary of deals where the seller cannot log into TIMS or show original documents. Keep copies of documents offered and the official search outcome.

title: Hit-and-run — general guidance
content: Leaving the scene of an accident is a serious offence. Victims should get medical care, report immediately, and preserve any dashcam, CCTV, plate fragments, and witness details. Do not chase dangerously; let police investigate.

title: Injury compensation after accidents — general guidance
content: Injury claims need medical reports, P3 forms, expense receipts, proof of lost income, and the police abstract. Limitation periods apply, so start early and verify deadlines with a lawyer. Keep a dated file of every bill and appointment.

title: NTSA inspection and vehicle condition — general guidance
content: Vehicles must be roadworthy, and inspection records can reveal condition and compliance issues. Ask when the vehicle was last inspected and whether any defects were noted. Keep inspection reports and repair receipts.

title: Motor insurance claims — general guidance
content: Notify your insurer quickly after an accident with the police abstract, photos, repair estimates, and medical reports. Third-party injury claims follow statutory procedures with strict evidence needs. Keep claim numbers and every submission receipt.

title: Compulsory motor insurance in Kenya — general guidance
citation: Insurance Act, Cap. 487; Traffic Act, Cap. 403
content: Every motor vehicle used on a public road must have at least third-party motor insurance from a licensed insurer. Driving without valid cover can lead to fines, impounding and personal liability for accident damage. Keep the insurance certificate, policy schedule and renewal receipts in the vehicle file.

title: Motor insurance when buying or selling a vehicle — general guidance
citation: Insurance Act, Cap. 487; Insurance Regulatory Authority guidance
content: Motor insurance does not automatically transfer with the logbook, so the new owner should arrange fresh cover before driving the vehicle. The seller should notify their insurer of the sale to stop future liability. Keep the new cover note, policy documents and cancellation or notification letters.

title: NTSA motor vehicle search before buying — general guidance
content: Before paying for a used car, do an NTSA search to confirm the registered owner, engine and chassis numbers, and whether any loan or caveat is recorded. Do not rely on a photocopy logbook or the seller's word alone. Keep the search result printout and the seller's ID details.

title: NTSA licensing and inspection — general guidance
citation: National Transport and Safety Authority Act, No. 33 of 2012
content: Driving licences, vehicle registration, inspection, and PSV licensing run through the National Transport and Safety Authority, increasingly online. Keep NTSA receipts, inspection stickers, and licence records for enforcement or accident follow-up.

title: Number plates and motor vehicle identity — general guidance
content: Registration plates should match the logbook and TIMS record, be properly fixed, and not be obscured or altered. Mismatched or temporary plates without documents are a warning sign. Keep photos of plates, chassis plates and the NTSA search.

title: PSV and boda boda incidents — general guidance
content: For matatu and boda boda incidents, record the registration, SACCO or stage, driver details, and route, plus photos and witness contacts. Report to police and the SACCO or owner, and notify the insurer. Keep treatment and fare or delivery records.

title: Stolen motor vehicle checks — general guidance
citation: Traffic Act, Cap. 403; National Police Service guidance
content: A stolen vehicle remains the property of the true owner even if you paid for it, and it can be recovered by police. Check that chassis and engine numbers are original and not tampered with, and verify ownership through NTSA. Keep search results, agreement copies and seller contacts.

title: First steps after any accident
content: Secure the scene, help the injured, call emergency services, and exchange details. Do not admit liability at the roadside. Keep photos, plates, and witness contacts.

title: P3 forms after road injuries
content: Police issue P3 forms for medical documentation of road injuries. Complete promptly and return to investigators. Keep hospital notes and OB numbers.

title: Drink-driving breath tests
content: Officers may require breath or blood tests where drink-driving is suspected. Refusal has legal consequences. Seek counsel early and note testing details.

title: Insurance assessors and repairs
content: Assessors inspect and approve repair estimates; do not authorise repairs before approval except to secure the vehicle. Keep estimates, approvals, and garage invoices.

title: Boda boda registration and stages
content: Riders need licences, protective gear, and stage registration with SACCO or association records. Keep licences, stage cards, and payment records.

title: Careless and dangerous driving charges
content: Charges grade from careless to dangerous with fines, licence consequences, and jail terms. Defences turn on road evidence and witnesses. Keep scene photos and charge sheets.

title: Cash bail at traffic stops
content: Minor traffic offences may attract cash bail with official receipts and a court date. Demand a receipt for any payment. Keep the bail receipt and charge sheet.

title: Chassis and engine number checks
content: Compare physical stampings with the logbook and TIMS; tampering voids the deal. Walk away where the seller resists verification. Keep search and inspection notes.

title: Notifying insurers after accidents
content: Notify the insurer promptly with abstract, photos, and estimates per policy timelines. Late notice risks repudiation. Keep claim numbers and submission receipts.

title: Pleading in traffic court
content: Understand the charge, consider plea options with counsel, and bring licence, insurance, and inspection documents. Keep the charge sheet and hearing dates.

title: Cyclist and motorbike rider claims
content: Rider claims follow the same abstract, P3, and medical evidence chain with helmet and licence context. Keep repair estimates and treatment records.

title: Fatal accident claims by dependants
citation: Fatal Accidents Act; Law Reform Act
content: Dependants claim lost support with death, dependency, and income evidence. File within limitation with grant and records. Keep OB, post-mortem, and income proof.

title: Choosing a driving school
content: Train at NTSA-licensed schools with written fees, lessons, and test booking terms. Keep receipts and training records.

title: Passengers and drink-driving liability
content: Passengers should avoid drunk drivers and report dangerous driving; owners face liability for entrusting vehicles. Keep trip and report records.

title: Replacing a lost driving licence
content: Lost licences need police abstract, application, and fees for replacement. Report loss promptly. Keep the abstract and application receipts.

title: Duty verification for imports
citation: EAC Customs Management Act; KRA guidance
content: Ask for import entries and duty receipts and verify registration before paying. Unpaid duty cars face seizure. Keep import and TIMS records.

title: Fake insurance stickers
content: Verify stickers with the insurer and IRA before driving off. Fake cover voids claims. Keep verification messages and policy documents.

title: Paying traffic fines officially
content: Pay fines through official court and government channels with receipts, never cash to individuals. Keep the ticket, receipt, and case reference.

title: Foreign licences in Kenya
content: Visitors drive on valid foreign or international permits within allowed periods; residents convert to Kenyan licences. Keep permits and entry records.

title: Helmet and safety gear offences
content: Riders and passengers must wear standard helmets with reflective gear at night. Fines follow non-compliance. Keep receipts for compliant gear.

title: Hit-and-run: victim steps
content: Get care, report immediately, and preserve dashcam, CCTV, fragments, and witness details. Do not chase dangerously. Keep OB and treatment records.

title: Third-party injury claims
citation: Insurance (Motor Vehicle Third Party Risks) Act
content: Injury claims need police abstract, P3 and medical reports, expense receipts, and lost-income proof within limitation periods. Start early with counsel. Keep every bill.

title: Motor vehicle inspection bookings
content: Commercial and PSV vehicles undergo periodic inspection for roadworthiness with stickers. Book early with registration documents. Keep inspection reports and stickers.

title: Driving licence classes in Kenya
content: Licences are classed by vehicle type with tests, medicals, and renewals per class. Drive only the endorsed class. Keep the licence, test records, and renewal receipts.

title: Licence endorsement and suspension
content: Repeat offences attract endorsements and suspension with hearing rights. Defend with records and counsel. Keep offence history and hearing notices.

title: Turnboys and loader injuries
citation: Work Injury Benefits Act; Traffic Act
content: Loader injuries need incident reports, treatment records, and employer compensation filings. Keep employment proof and medical files.

title: Boda loans and repossession
content: Boda hire-purchase needs statements, instalment proof, and repossession notices. Demand the arrears figure in writing. Keep agreements and payment records.

title: New car registration (scratch to plates)
content: Dealers handle KRA duty, registration, and plates with logbook processing. Verify TIMS records before driving off. Keep sale, duty, and registration records.

title: Number plate verification
content: Plates must match the logbook and TIMS record, properly fixed and unobscured. Mismatches signal fraud. Keep plate photos and the search result.

title: Obstruction and illegal parking
content: Obstructing traffic or parking illegally attracts fines, clamping, and towing. Pay through official channels with receipts. Keep the ticket and payment proof.

title: Overloading fines
content: Overloaded lorries face weighbridge fines and offloading with owner and driver liability. Verify load sheets. Keep weighbridge tickets and charge sheets.

title: Own-damage (comprehensive) claims
content: Comprehensive claims need the policy schedule, abstract, and repair evidence with excess deducted. Confirm exclusions like drink-driving. Keep the full claim file.

title: Passenger rights after accidents
content: Passengers claim against the at-fault vehicle cover with tickets, treatment records, and the abstract. Record the plate and SACCO. Keep fare proof and medical files.

title: Pedestrian knock-down claims
content: Pedestrian claims need the abstract, treatment records, and witness details with the offending plate. Report promptly. Keep every medical receipt.

title: Phone use while driving
content: Holding a phone while driving attracts fines and licence action. Use hands-free mounts. Keep the ticket where disputing the facts.

title: Accidents with convoys and GK vehicles
content: Record plate, unit markings, time, and witnesses, then report to police for abstract processing. Claims follow government procedure. Keep OB and treatment records.

title: PSV licensing and SACCO membership
content: PSVs need operator licences, SACCO or company affiliation, and compliant crew with badges. Verify documents before investing. Keep licences and agreements.

title: Renewing driving licences
content: Renew before expiry through NTSA channels to avoid penalties and enforcement. Keep renewal receipts with the licence.

title: Motor sale agreements checklist
content: Agreements record IDs, registration, engine and chassis numbers, price, schedule, and handover with witnesses. Both sides sign. Keep copies and payment receipts.

title: School transport compliance
content: School vans need yellow paint, speed governors, attendants, and vetted drivers with no overloading. Report violations with photos. Keep contracts and fee receipts.

title: Seat belt offences
content: Drivers and passengers must wear belts where fitted. Fines apply per occupant. Keep the charge sheet where disputing fitting or use.

title: Smart driving licence applications
content: Smart licences apply through NTSA with biometrics, medical, and fees. Book early and track the application. Keep booking slips and payment receipts.

title: Speed limits and cameras
content: Limits vary by road class and vehicle type with camera and NTSA enforcement. Fines and licence action follow readings. Keep the charge sheet and calibration queries for counsel.

title: Taxi licensing basics
content: Taxis need registration, inspection, insurance, and licensed drivers with fare transparency. Keep permits and inspection records.

title: Driving test bookings
content: Tests book through NTSA with ID, training proof, and fees. Prepare documents and practise the route. Keep booking slips and results.

title: TIMS transfer step by step
content: The seller initiates transfer, the buyer accepts, fees are paid officially, and a new logbook issues. Both need eCitizen and TIMS accounts. Keep sale, payment, ID, and receipt records.

title: Towed vehicles: recovery steps
content: Locate the yard, verify the offence and fees, pay officially, and inspect for damage before leaving. Keep the ticket, payment receipts, and yard records.

title: Tuk-tuk operating requirements
content: Tuk-tuks need registration, inspection, insurance, and licensed drivers on authorised routes. Keep permits and fee receipts.

title: Driving without insurance
content: Every public-road vehicle needs at least third-party cover; driving uninsured risks fines, impound, and personal liability. Keep the cover note and policy.

title: Driving without a licence
content: Driving unlicensed or outside the endorsed class risks fines, vehicle detention, and insurance repudiation. Get the correct class before driving. Keep test and licence records.

title: Total loss and write-off settlements
content: Write-offs settle on market value less excess and salvage per policy. Compare valuations before accepting. Keep valuation reports and settlement letters.

title: Traffic Act — overview
content: The Traffic Act regulates licensing, vehicle inspection, speed, drink-driving, and careless or dangerous driving, with fines, licence consequences, and possible imprisonment. After any incident, prioritise safety and medical care, then comply with police directions. Keep licence, inspection, and insurance documents.
